title: The RP2A0X APU registers in MAME
covers: the twenty-three CPU ports of the Ricoh RP2A0X audio processing unit as MAME's nes_apu device handles them; no official document was found

searched.gave: The header of nes_apu.cpp names Matthew Conte's Nofrendo core, its authors and timing notes, and cites no document.
A web search for a Ricoh RP2A03 or 2A03 datasheet found no page of Ricoh or Nintendo holding one.
The ricoh folder under components holds two data books, 1988 and 1993; neither names the 2A03, the RP2A or the 2A07.
Searches for RP2A03 and for 2A03 found community write-ups and die analyses, no maker document.
datasheetarchive.com answered a search for 2A03 with unrelated components and no Ricoh document.

rows.text: Port 0x4000 is square 1's first register; a write stores the byte in the channel's regs[0].
Bits 0-3 choose the envelope step interval: the table's entry for the low nibble is the delay between steps.
Bit 4 selects a fixed volume: set, the channel outputs bits 0-3 instead of the decayed level.
Bit 5 loops the envelope, which then adds one and wraps to 0 at 16, and it holds the length counter.
Bits 6-7 select one of four duty patterns, and the pattern's bit chosen by bits 1-3 of the adder multiplies the output.
Each step raises the decayed level by one until 15; a length write on an enabled channel starts it again at 0.
With bit 5 clear each call decrements the length counter, and at zero the channel's output is 0.
The core maps 0x4000-0x4013 to write, so port 0x4000 arrives as offset 0x00.
Port 0x4004 is square 2's first register; a write stores the byte in the channel's regs[0].
Bits 0-3 choose the envelope step interval: the table's entry for the low nibble is the delay between steps.
Bit 4 selects a fixed volume: set, the channel outputs bits 0-3 instead of the decayed level.
Bit 5 loops the envelope, which then adds one and wraps to 0 at 16, and it holds the length counter.
Bits 6-7 select one of four duty patterns, and the pattern's bit chosen by bits 1-3 of the adder multiplies the output.
Each step raises the decayed level by one until 15; a length write on an enabled channel starts it again at 0.
With bit 5 clear each call decrements the length counter, and at zero the channel's output is 0.
Port 0x4001 is square 1's sweep register; a write stores the byte in the channel's regs[1].
A write stores the byte in the channel's register.
The sweep runs only while bit 7 is set and the low three bits are nonzero.
Bit 3 chooses the direction: set, the frequency value falls by its own shifted part; clear, it rises, and a larger value is a longer period.
Bits 4-6 index the sync table for the delay between the sweep's steps.
Bits 0-2 are the shift count, so one step changes the period by one part in a power of two.
The channel goes silent when the period falls below 4, or, with bit 3 clear, once it passes the limit for the low three bits.
Port 0x4005 is square 2's sweep register; a write stores the byte in the channel's regs[1].
A write stores the byte in the channel's register.
The sweep runs only while bit 7 is set and the low three bits are nonzero.
Bit 3 chooses the direction: set, the frequency value falls by its own shifted part; clear, it rises, and a larger value is a longer period.
Bits 4-6 index the sync table for the delay between the sweep's steps.
Bits 0-2 are the shift count, so one step changes the period by one part in a power of two.
The channel goes silent when the period falls below 4, or, with bit 3 clear, once it passes the limit for the low three bits.
Port 0x4002 is the low byte of square 1's 11-bit period.
When the channel is enabled a write rebuilds the period from the high bits, this byte, plus one, shifted 16 places.
While the channel is disabled the byte is only stored; the period waits for the next recomputation.
Port 0x4006 is the low byte of square 2's 11-bit period.
When the channel is enabled a write rebuilds the period from the high bits, this byte, plus one, shifted 16 places.
While the channel is disabled the byte is only stored; the period waits for the next recomputation.
Port 0x4003 carries the high three bits of square 1's period and the length index.
When the channel is enabled a write loads the length from the top five bits, restarts the envelope at 0 and rebuilds the period.
Bits 0-2 are the period's high bits and bits 3-7 index a thirty-two entry length table.
The loaded length is the table's value times half the samples of a sync, so the table is scaled to the renderer's rate.
Port 0x4007 carries the high three bits of square 2's period and the length index.
When the channel is enabled a write loads the length from the top five bits, restarts the envelope at 0 and rebuilds the period.
Bits 0-2 are the period's high bits and bits 3-7 index a thirty-two entry length table.
The loaded length is the table's value times half the samples of a sync, so the table is scaled to the renderer's rate.
Port 0x4008 is the triangle's first register; a write stores the byte in the channel's regs[0].
While the channel is enabled and the counter has not started, a write loads the linear length from the low seven bits.
Bit 7 holds the counter: while it is set the reload flag is not cleared, so once the counter starts every renderer call reloads the linear length.
Bits 0-6 index the sync table that gives the linear length.
The counter starts on the first renderer call that finds bit 7 of 0x4008 clear, once any latency set by a 0x400B write has run out.
Port 0x4009 is unused: the case compares the offset with 0x4009, while the address map passes this port as offset 0x09.
A write to port 0x4009 reaches the default case, which only logs under a debug build; the triangle's second register stays as it was.
The case, were it reached, would store the byte in the triangle's second register, which the header marks unused.
Port 0x400A is the low byte of the triangle's 11-bit period.
A write only stores the byte; the renderer rebuilds the period from both bytes each sample.
The period is the eleven bits plus one, and a period of 1 returns before the phase moves.
A period below two returns before the phase moves, so the channel's output holds its last value.
Port 0x400B carries the triangle's period high bits and its length index; a write stores the byte.
A write sets a latency of a 240th of a frame, counted in renderer calls, during which the linear counter cannot start.
While the channel is enabled the write clears the start flag, loads the length, reloads the linear length and marks the reload.
Bits 0-2 extend the period above the low byte and bits 3-7 index the length table.
Port 0x400C is the noise channel's first register; a write stores the byte in the channel's regs[0].
A write stores the byte in the channel's register.
Bits 0-3 choose the envelope step interval from the sync table.
Bit 4 makes the volume fixed: the channel outputs bits 0-3 instead of the decayed level.
Bit 5 loops the envelope and stops the length counter from counting down.
With bit 5 clear each call decrements the length counter, and at zero the channel's output is 0.
Port 0x400D is unused: the case compares the offset with 0x400D, while the address map passes this port as offset 0x0D.
A write to port 0x400D reaches the default case, which only logs under a debug build; the noise's second register stays as it was.
The case, were it reached, would store the byte in the noise's second register, which the header marks unused.
Port 0x400E holds the noise period and the sequence-mode flag; a write stores the byte.
A write stores the byte in the channel's register.
Bits 0-3 index a period table, which has a PAL variant selected by the device's clock.
Bit 7 selects the shift tap: six, for the small 93-byte sample, when set, and one when clear.
The RP2A03 subclass ignores bit 7 and always shifts with tap one, so the flag changes nothing on that device.
Port 0x400F holds the noise length index and a write stores the byte.
While the channel is enabled a write loads the length from the top five bits and resets the envelope volume.
The length load shifts the byte right three places, so its top five bits choose the table entry.
Port 0x4010 is the DMC's control register; a write stores the byte.
A write stores the byte in the channel's register.
Bit 7 enables the DMC's interrupt at the end of a sample; clearing it drops the pending request.
Bit 6 loops the sample: at the end of the length the address and length are reloaded instead of stopping.
Bits 0-3 index the clock table that sets the DMC's output rate, one table for NTSC and one for PAL.
A write with bit 7 clear also clears the DMC interrupt flag and, when no frame interrupt is pending, lowers the line.
Port 0x4011 sets the DMC's output level; a write keeps the low seven bits of the byte.
The stored level is the accumulator that each bit of the sample moves by two.
A set bit raises the level by two while it is at most 125; otherwise, and at 2 or above, it falls by two, staying within 0 and 127.
Port 0x4012 holds the DMC sample address in 64-byte units, counted from 0xC000.
A write stores the byte; the address is rebuilt at 0xC000 plus 64 times it when the channel starts or loops.
Port 0x4013 holds the DMC sample length in 16-byte units plus one.
A write stores the byte; the length and its bit count are rebuilt when the channel starts or loops.
A write to port 0x4015 enables the four tone channels and the DMC, one bit each.
A write stores no register value; clearing a channel's bit stops it and zeroes the length counters it holds.
Bits 0-3 enable the two squares, the triangle and the noise; clearing one stops it and zeroes its length counters.
Bit 4 enables the DMC: when it was disabled, a write reloads the address, the length and its bit count, and marks the channel enabled.
Clearing bit 4 stops the DMC and leaves the address and length it had.
A write clears the DMC interrupt flag and, when no frame interrupt is pending, lowers the interrupt line.
The core maps 0x4015's write to a lambda that calls write with offset 0x15.
A read of port 0x4015 reports the channels whose length counters run, the DMC's enable and the two interrupt flags.
Bits 0-3 are set when a square, the triangle or the noise holds a nonzero length; bit 4 follows the DMC's enable.
Bit 6 reports the frame interrupt and bit 7 the DMC's, and the read clears the frame flag.
A read also lowers the interrupt line when no DMC interrupt is pending.
The driver maps port 0x4015's read to status_r and its write to a lambda that calls write with offset 0x15.
Port 0x4017 selects the frame sequencer's step mode and its interrupt.
A write stores no register of its own: the byte sets the step mode and the interrupt enable in the device's state.
Bit 7 selects the five-step mode and clearing it selects four steps.
Bit 6 inhibits the frame interrupt: set, the timer stops and the pending flag clears; clear, the timer is rearmed each period.
The timer callback raises the frame interrupt only when the mode is four steps and the interrupt is enabled.
The frame timer counts 29830 clocks for NTSC and 33254 for PAL, converted at the device's clock rate.
The core maps 0x4017's write to a lambda that calls write with offset 0x17.
